title: Are these graphics comfortable to look at?
author: fardwyn

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body:
Not sure what you mean "graphics", but there's multiple problems
Parallax is not parallaxing. Make it 20% wider and set the parallax to approximately the width of your level. Fix the zooming parallax issues too. Those cause eyes pain

The animations are weak. In the world of AI assets, animations is your best friend, because they're not too hard and they make generic AI character to look vivid and juicy.

The colors of background are okay, but the character itself receives a color from surrounding. Blends in too much. Maybe metallic param is too high? It's too reflective. I dunno, i'm not expert and just don't like it. Ideally, you'd have every character and enemy easily distinctive from surrounding.

replies.author: fardwyn
replies.body: My main question was for the pixelarion effect. Im using a "dumb" method of just bringing down the resolution woth a sub viewport no extra effort. I was wondering if it looked good or if i would need to add more stuff like fixed grid or something

replies.author: unfamily_friendly
replies.body:
Oh i understand. You making fake pixel art by nearest scaling the 3D models. Kinda like in Dead Cell

Iirc, they're not doing it in real time. They pre baked all the graphics for characters. It's all 2D screenshots of 3D models, pixelated and slightly eddited. This gives better performance and more control

comments.author: AshlaStudios
comments.body:
Health bars are a big issue and ruin the visuals, fix them asap.

Someone already mentioned parallax issues so fix that too.

Make animations procedural so they dont feel so repetitive.

**I love the transition from area A to B, do more stuff like this, really elevates the feel of the game.**
